children: Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd (HAL) is set to deliver the first batch of delayed HTT-40 basic trainer aircraft to the Indian Air Force (IAF), helping meet its growing requirement for pilot training, a Hindustan Times report said on Monday.
Three HTT-40 (Hindustan Turbo Trainer-40) aircraft - two built in Bengaluru and one in Nashik - are ready for delivery, officials aware of the development told the newspaper.
HAL shares were up 0.74% at Rs 4,891 on the NSE at 9:15 am on Monday, gaining Rs 35.90.

The IAF had ordered 70 HTT-40 aircraft from HAL for Rs 6,838 crore in 2023 to train rookie pilots. HAL was required to deliver 12 aircraft during 2025-26 but could not deliver any due to a shortage of engines.

The delay was linked to supply chain bottlenecks faced by US-based Honeywell, which supplies the TPE331-12B turboprop engines for the aircraft. Honeywell delivered the first batch of engines a few months ago and assured HAL of timely supplies.

Under a $100 million contract signed four years ago for 88 TPE331-12B engines and kits, Honeywell was supposed to deliver the first engine in September 2025. The US company will supply 16 engines, while HAL will manufacture the remaining units under a technology transfer arrangement.

Defence Minister Rajnath Singh inaugurated HTT-40 and LCA-Mk1A production lines at HAL's Nashik facility in October last year. HAL can now manufacture up to 20 HTT-40 aircraft annually across its Bengaluru and Nashik facilities.

At present, all rookie IAF pilots undergo Stage-I, or ab initio, flying training on Swiss-origin Pilatus PC-7 MkII basic trainers. After this common stage, pilots are divided into fighter, transport and helicopter streams.
Fighter pilots undergo Stage-II training on the PC-7 MkII and Kiran Mk-1A jet trainers, followed by Stage-III training on British-origin Hawk advanced jet trainers.

title: Hindustan Aeronautics set to deliver first batch of delayed HTT-40 trainer aircraft to IAF, share up nearly 1%
